evals.prompt: Run /codebase-doctor and check the quality of this project.
evals.expected_output: Stack detection, a verdict for every check, score calculation, report file generation, fix proposals, and a request for user review
expectations: Stack detection states four elements: language, framework, project type and components
It reads CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md and reflects the rules written there in the criteria of subsequent checks
Check 1 (AI Agent Guidelines) runs before the other checks
Each check is explicitly given one of PASS/WARN/FAIL/SKIP
The terminal output follows the format starting with '=== Codebase Doctor Report ==='
The score calculation excludes SKIP from the denominator
The score calculation counts WARN as 0.5
The score is shown in X/Y form (e.g. 5/7)
A .md file with a YYYYMMDDHHmmss timestamp is generated under .context/doctor/
The report has four sections: Summary, Detailed Findings, Fix Proposals, User Review
Each FAIL/WARN item has a fix proposal with What, Where and How
It does not auto-apply fixes and asks the user for approval
If Testing is FAIL, the other check results carry the [*] suffix

evals.prompt: Please check the quality of this codebase. I want to confirm the basic features are in place.
evals.expected_output: Even without naming the command directly, the codebase-doctor skill triggers and runs equivalent checks
expectations: The audit follows the codebase-doctor workflow (Detect → Select → Run → Report → Propose → Review)
The skill triggers correctly even without an explicit /codebase-doctor command
The rg-syntax patterns in check-patterns.md (| for OR search) are used
The [inferred] mark is used for unsupported languages (if applicable)

evals.prompt: Run codebase-doctor with the evals/files/python-fastapi/ directory as the project root.
evals.expected_output: The Python/FastAPI/SQLite stack is detected, conditional checks (Migration, API Error, Input Validation, Security) fire, and the intentional problems are detected correctly
expectations: Stack detection: Python, FastAPI and SQLite (or a DB) are detected
Check 1 (AI Agent Guidelines): FAIL — no CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md exists
Check 2 (Logging): FAIL — points out that logging/structlog is not used and print() is used instead
Check 3 (Error Handling): FAIL — detects the swallowed error in except: pass
Check 4 (Configuration): PASS or WARN — detects config read via os.environ
Check 6 (Testing): FAIL — no test files exist
Check 7 (Dependency Lock): FAIL — no poetry.lock/Pipfile.lock/uv.lock exists (requirements.txt is not treated as a lock file)
Check 8 (Database Migrations): FAIL — detects no migration tool and a direct CREATE TABLE
Check 9 (Input Validation): FAIL or WARN — the endpoints have no validation
Check 10 (API Error Responses): FAIL or WARN — error responses are inconsistent
Check 11 (Security): FAIL — detects SQL string concatenation (SQL injection vulnerability)
Because Testing is FAIL, the other checks carry the [*] suffix
Graceful Shutdown (Check 5) is FAIL, not SKIP — it is a server app yet has no signal handling

evals.prompt: Run codebase-doctor with the evals/files/nextjs-frontend/ directory as the project root.
evals.expected_output: The TypeScript/Next.js stack is detected, DB/API checks are SKIP, and the CLAUDE.md rule violation (console.log) is detected
expectations: Stack detection: TypeScript, Next.js and a web UI are detected
Check 1 (AI Agent Guidelines): PASS or WARN — CLAUDE.md exists and defines the tech stack and conventions (WARN is also acceptable if commands are missing)
The CLAUDE.md rule 'Do not use console.log' is reflected in the calibration of subsequent checks
Check 2 (Logging): WARN or FAIL — points out that page.tsx uses console.log, which CLAUDE.md forbids (FAIL is also acceptable if no alternative library is installed)
Check 6 (Testing): PASS — test files exist and jest is configured
Check 7 (Dependency Lock): PASS — package-lock.json exists
Check 8 (Database Migrations): SKIP — no DB detected
Check 10 (API Error Responses): SKIP — no HTTP API endpoints (app/api/) exist
Skipped checks are excluded from the score's denominator
The score's denominator is not all 11 checks but the number excluding SKIP

evals.prompt: Run codebase-doctor with the evals/files/no-guidelines/ directory as the project root.
evals.expected_output: The Node.js/Express stack is detected, the Check 1 FAIL affects subsequent checks, and the intentional problems (empty catch, inconsistent error responses) are detected
expectations: Stack detection: JavaScript, Express and an HTTP API are detected
Check 1 (AI Agent Guidelines): FAIL — none of CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md/.cursorrules exists
Because Check 1 is FAIL, it mentions that subsequent checks use generic patterns rather than project-specific rules (e.g. 'No project guidelines found — checks use generic patterns')
Check 2 (Logging): PASS — detects structured logging with winston
Check 3 (Error Handling): FAIL — detects the empty catch block
Check 4 (Configuration): PASS or WARN — detects config read via process.env
Check 5 (Graceful Shutdown): PASS — detects process.on('SIGTERM')
Check 6 (Testing): PASS or WARN — test files exist but are thin
Check 7 (Dependency Lock): PASS — package-lock.json exists
Check 8 (Database Migrations): SKIP — no DB detected
Check 10 (API Error Responses): FAIL or WARN — detects the res.status(200).send('error:...') anti-pattern, or points out inconsistent status codes
Check 9 (Input Validation): FAIL or WARN — the API endpoints have no validation

evals.prompt: テストフェーズにはいるのでプロジェクト設定を見直してほしい。
evals.expected_output: phase=test is determined, the test-related checks (6/9/10/12/13) are weighted, and test-oriented project-scoped skills and permissions for test commands are proposed. The prompt is in Japanese on purpose, to cover the Japanese trigger phrases in the description
expectations: It gives the user's explicit statement priority, determines phase=test, and the report has a Phase line
Check 12 verifies whether the test commands are in permissions.allow
When Check 13 decides whether testing skills are needed, it first consults the user's skill catalog (if any)
The skill install command has no -g (project scope)
Implementation quality checks still run, but their fix proposals get lower priority than the test-phase items

evals.prompt: I just created this repository. Please look at the initial setup with /codebase-doctor.
evals.expected_output: phase=setup is determined, and CLAUDE.md, permissions and stack-matched skills get the focus. Hooks are SKIP because there is no repeated pattern
expectations: It infers phase=setup from the commit count, whether tests exist and whether CI exists
Check 1 (AI Agent Guidelines) is reported as FAIL or WARN
Check 14 (Hooks) is SKIP, with the absence of repeated patterns given as the reason
Check 15 (Remote Execution) is SKIP because remote execution is not intended

evals.prompt: I just put the settings in, but please review the project settings once more.
evals.expected_output: Items already satisfied are reported as PASS, and no fix proposals are made for them (idempotent)
expectations: It reads the existing .claude/settings.json and installed skills first
It does not propose reinstalling skills that are already installed
It does not propose overwriting existing permissions entries or CLAUDE.md (proposes additions only)
For items that have not changed, it states they are 'already PASS', and the proposal list is empty or nearly so
